tool.name: ProteomicsLFQ
tool.command:
@QUOTE_FOO@ @EXT_FOO@ #import re
## Preprocessing #if $in_cond.in: mkdir in_cond.in && #if $in_cond.in_select == "no" mkdir ${' '.join(["'in_cond.in/%s'" % (i) for i, f in enumerate($in_cond.in) if f])} && ${' '.join(["cp '%s' 'in_cond.in/%s/%s' && " % (f, i, $gxy_input_basename(f.element_identifier, f.ext)) for i, f in enumerate($in_cond.in) if f])} #else cp '$in_cond.in' 'in_cond.in/${gxy_input_basename($in_cond.in.element_identifier, $in_cond.in.ext)}' && #end if #end if #if $ids_cond.ids: mkdir ids_cond.ids && #if $ids_cond.ids_select == "no" mkdir ${' '.join(["'ids_cond.ids/%s'" % (i) for i, f in enumerate($ids_cond.ids) if f])} && ${' '.join(["cp '%s' 'ids_cond.ids/%s/%s' && " % (f, i, $gxy_input_basename(f.element_identifier, f.ext)) for i, f in enumerate($ids_cond.ids) if f])} #else cp '$ids_cond.ids' 'ids_cond.ids/${gxy_input_basename($ids_cond.ids.element_identifier, $ids_cond.ids.ext)}' && #end if #end if #if $design: mkdir design && cp '$design' 'design/${gxy_input_basename($design.element_identifier, $design.ext)}' && #end if #if $fasta: mkdir fasta && cp '$fasta' 'fasta/${gxy_input_basename($fasta.element_identifier, $fasta.ext)}' && #end if #if "out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out && #end if #if "out_msstats_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_msstats && #end if #if "out_cxml_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_cxml && #end if #if "out_qpx_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_qpx && #end if #if "feat_dir_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir feat_dir && #end if #if "candidates_out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir PeptideQuantification_candidates_out && #end if
## Main program call
set -o pipefail && @EXECUTABLE@ -write_ctd ./ && python3 '$__tool_directory__/fill_ctd.py' '@EXECUTABLE@.ctd' '$args_json' '$hardcoded_json' && @EXECUTABLE@ -ini @EXECUTABLE@.ctd #if $in_cond.in: -in #if $in_cond.in_select == "no" ${' '.join(["'in_cond.in/%s/%s'"%(i, $gxy_input_basename(f.element_identifier, f.ext)) for i, f in enumerate($in_cond.in) if f])} #else 'in_cond.in/${gxy_input_basename($in_cond.in.element_identifier, $in_cond.in.ext)}' #end if #end if #if $ids_cond.ids: -ids #if $ids_cond.ids_select == "no" ${' '.join(["'ids_cond.ids/%s/%s'"%(i, $gxy_input_basename(f.element_identifier, f.ext)) for i, f in enumerate($ids_cond.ids) if f])} #else 'ids_cond.ids/${gxy_input_basename($ids_cond.ids.element_identifier, $ids_cond.ids.ext)}' #end if #end if #if $design: -design 'design/${gxy_input_basename($design.element_identifier, $design.ext)}' #end if #if $fasta: -fasta 'fasta/${gxy_input_basename($fasta.element_identifier, $fasta.ext)}' #end if #if "out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out 'out/output.${gxy2omsext("mztab")}' #end if #if "out_msstats_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_msstats 'out_msstats/output.${gxy2omsext("csv")}' #end if #if "out_cxml_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_cxml 'out_cxml/output.${gxy2omsext("consensusxml")}' #end if #if "out_qpx_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_qpx out_qpx/ #end if #if "feat_dir_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -feat_dir feat_dir/ #end if #if "candidates_out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -PeptideQuantification:candidates_out 'PeptideQuantification_candidates_out/output.${gxy2omsext("txt")}' #end if #if len(str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',')) == 0 | tee '$stdout' #end if
## Postprocessing #if "out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out/output.${gxy2omsext("mztab")}' '$out' #end if #if "out_msstats_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out_msstats/output.${gxy2omsext("csv")}' '$out_msstats' #end if #if "out_cxml_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out_cxml/output.${gxy2omsext("consensusxml")}' '$out_cxml' #end if #if "candidates_out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'PeptideQuantification_candidates_out/output.${gxy2omsext("txt")}' '$PeptideQuantification_candidates_out' #end if #if "ctd_out_FLAG" in $OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS && mv '@EXECUTABLE@.ctd' '$ctd_out' #end if

section.name: Seeding
section.title: Parameters for seeding of untargeted features

param.name: intThreshold
param.label: Peak intensity threshold applied in seed detection

param.name: charge
param.label: Charge range considered for untargeted feature seeds

param.name: traceRTTolerance
param.label: Combines all spectra in the tolerance window to stabilize identification of isotope patterns
param.help: Controls sensitivity (low value) vs. specificity (high value) of feature seeds

param.name: algorithm
param.label: Algorithm for untargeted seed feature detection
param.help: multiplex: FeatureFinderMultiplexAlgorithm (default, current behavior).. biosaur2: Biosaur2Algorithm (handles IM_PEAK/PASEF data natively)

param.name: mini
param.label: Minimum intensity threshold

param.name: minmz
param.label: Minimum m/z value

param.name: maxmz
param.label: Maximum m/z value

param.name: htol
param.label: Mass accuracy in ppm for combining peaks into hills

param.name: itol
param.label: Mass accuracy in ppm for isotopic patterns

param.name: hvf
param.label: Hill valley factor for splitting hills

param.name: ivf
param.label: Isotope valley factor for splitting isotope patterns

param.name: minlh
param.label: Minimum number of scans for a hill

param.name: pasefmini
param.label: Minimum combined intensity for PASEF/TIMS clusters after m/z–ion-mobility centroiding

param.name: pasefminlh
param.label: Minimum number of raw points per PASEF/TIMS cluster during centroiding

param.name: cmin
param.label: Minimum charge state

param.name: cmax
param.label: Maximum charge state

param.name: iuse
param.label: Number of isotopes for intensity calculation (0=mono only, -1=all, 1=mono+first, etc.)

param.name: nm
param.label: Negative mode (affects neutral mass calculation)

param.name: tof
param.label: Enable TOF-specific intensity filtering

param.name: profile
param.label: Enable profile mode processing (centroid spectra using PeakPickerHiRes)

param.name: paseftol
param.label: Ion mobility accuracy for linking peaks into hills and grouping isotopes (0 = disable IM-based gating)
param.help: Default is for 1/K0 units (e.g., 0.03-0.08). For CCS data, use larger values (e.g., 5-20 square angstroms)

param.name: use_hill_calib
param.label: Enable automatic hill mass tolerance calibration

param.name: ignore_iso_calib
param.label: Disable automatic isotope mass error calibration

param.name: hrttol
param.label: Maximum allowed RT difference (in seconds) between monoisotopic hill apex and isotope hill apex when assembling isotope patterns (0 disables RT gating)

param.name: convex_hulls
param.label: Representation of feature convex hulls in the output FeatureMap
param.help: 'bounding_box' stores a single RT–m/z bounding box per feature (smaller featureXML, no per-trace detail), whereas 'mass_traces' stores one convex hull per contributing hill using all mass-trace points (larger featureXML, preserves detailed trace shape)

param.name: faims_merge_features
param.label: For FAIMS data with multiple compensation voltages: Merge features representing the same analyte detected at different CV values into a single feature
param.help: Only features with DIFFERENT FAIMS CV values are merged (same CV = different analytes). Has no effect on non-FAIMS data

param.name: signal_to_noise
param.label: Minimal signal-to-noise ratio for a peak to be picked (0.0 disables SNT estimation!)

param.name: spacing_difference_gap
param.label: The extension of a peak is stopped if the spacing between two subsequent data points exceeds 'spacing_difference_gap * min_spacing'
param.help: 'min_spacing' is the smaller of the two spacings from the peak apex to its two neighboring points. '0' to disable the constraint. Not applicable to chromatograms

param.name: spacing_difference
param.label: Maximum allowed difference between points during peak extension, in multiples of the minimal difference between the peak apex and its two neighboring points
param.help: If this difference is exceeded a missing point is assumed (see parameter 'missing'). A higher value implies a less stringent peak definition, since individual signals within the peak are allowed to be further apart. '0' to disable the constraint. Not applicable to chromatograms

param.name: missing
param.label: Maximum number of missing points allowed when extending a peak to the left or to the right
param.help: A missing data point occurs if the spacing between two subsequent data points exceeds 'spacing_difference * min_spacing'. 'min_spacing' is the smaller of the two spacings from the peak apex to its two neighboring points. Not applicable to chromatograms

param.name: ms_levels
param.label: List of MS levels for which the peak picking is applied
param.help: If empty, auto mode is enabled, all peaks which aren't picked yet will get picked. Other scans are copied to the output without changes (space separated list, in order to allow for spaces in list items surround them by single quotes)

expand.name: ms_levels

validator.message: a space separated list of integer values in the range 1: is required

expand.validator: len(value.split(' ')) == len([_ for _ in value.split(' ') if 1 <= int(_)])

param.name: report_FWHM
param.label: Add metadata for FWHM (as floatDataArray named 'FWHM' or 'FWHM_ppm', depending on param 'report_FWHM_unit') for each picked peak

param.name: report_FWHM_unit
param.label: Unit of FWHM
param.help: Either absolute in the unit of input, e.g. 'm/z' for spectra, or relative as ppm (only sensible for spectra, not chromatograms)

param.name: allow_missing_flank
param.label: Allow peaks without flanking data points on both sides
param.help: This is useful for TimsTOF data where profile peaks may be missing the leading or trailing edge

param.name: max_intensity
param.label: maximal intensity considered for histogram construction
param.help: By default, it will be calculated automatically (see auto_mode). Only provide this parameter if you know what you are doing (and change 'auto_mode' to '-1')! All intensities EQUAL/ABOVE 'max_intensity' will be added to the LAST histogram bin. If you choose 'max_intensity' too small, the noise estimate might be too small as well. If chosen too big, the bins become quite large (which you could counter by increasing 'bin_count', which increases runtime). In general, the Median-S/N estimator is more robust to a manual max_intensity than the MeanIterative-S/N

param.name: auto_max_stdev_factor
param.label: parameter for 'max_intensity' estimation (if 'auto_mode' == 0): mean + 'auto_max_stdev_factor' * stdev

param.name: auto_max_percentile
param.label: parameter for 'max_intensity' estimation (if 'auto_mode' == 1): auto_max_percentile th percentile

param.name: auto_mode
param.label: method to use to determine maximal intensity: -1 --> use 'max_intensity'; 0 --> 'auto_max_stdev_factor' method (default); 1 --> 'auto_max_percentile' method

param.name: win_len
param.label: window length in Thomson

param.name: bin_count
param.label: number of bins for intensity values

param.name: min_required_elements
param.label: minimum number of elements required in a window (otherwise it is considered sparse)

param.name: noise_for_empty_window
param.label: noise value used for sparse windows

param.name: write_log_messages
param.label: Write out log messages in case of sparse windows or median in rightmost histogram bin

param.name: debug
param.label: Debug level for feature detection

param.name: quantify_decoys
param.label: Whether decoy peptides should be quantified (true) or skipped (false)

param.name: min_psm_cutoff
param.label: Minimum score for the best PSM of a spectrum to be used as seed
param.help: Use 'none' for no cutoff

param.name: add_mass_offset_peptides
param.label: If for every peptide (or seed) also an offset peptide is extracted (true)
param.help: Can be used to downstream to determine MBR false transfer rates. (0.0 = disabled)

param.name: seed_apex_rt_tolerance
param.label: Maximum allowed RT deviation (in seconds) between a seed's apex and the detected feature's apex
param.help: Seed-derived features whose detected apex deviates more than this value from the original seed apex are removed during filtering. Useful to discard unreliable seed extractions where the picked peak is far from the seed location. (0 = disabled)

param.name: batch_size
param.label: Nr of peptides used in each batch of chromatogram extraction
param.help: Smaller values decrease memory usage but increase runtime

param.name: mz_window
param.label: m/z window size for chromatogram extraction (unit: ppm if 1 or greater, else Da/Th)

param.name: IM_window
param.label: Ion mobility (IM) window for chromatogram extraction in the IM dimension
param.help: Set to 0.0 to disable IM filtering (even if data contains IM information). The window is applied as +/- IM_window/2 around the median IM value of identified peptides. This parameter is automatically ignored if the input data does not contain IM information (determined via IMTypes::determineIMFormat). Currently only concatenated IM format is supported. Typical values: 0.05-0.10 for TIMS data (1/K0 units), 10-50 for CCS data (square angstroms), 3-5 for FAIMS data (compensation voltage).Note: IM values are calculated per peptide/charge/RT-region, using the median of all identifications in that region for robustness. The median, min, and max IM values are propagated to output features as meta-values (IM_median, IM_min, IM_max) for quality control

param.name: n_isotopes
param.label: Number of isotopes to include in each peptide assay

param.name: isotope_pmin
param.label: Minimum probability for an isotope to be included in the assay for a peptide
param.help: If set, this parameter takes precedence over 'extract:n_isotopes'

param.name: rt_window
param.label: RT window size (in sec.) for chromatogram extraction
param.help: If not set, it is derived from 'detect:peak_width' and 'detect:mapping_tolerance'

section.name: detect
section.title: Parameters for detecting features in extracted ion chromatograms

param.name: min_peak_width
param.label: Minimum elution peak width
param.help: Absolute value in seconds if 1 or greater, else relative to 'peak_width'

param.name: signal_to_noise
param.label: Signal-to-noise threshold for OpenSWATH feature detection

param.name: mapping_tolerance
param.label: RT tolerance (plus/minus) for mapping peptide IDs to features
param.help: Absolute value in seconds if 1 or greater, else relative to the RT span of the feature

section.name: model
section.title: Parameters for fitting elution models to features

param.name: type
param.label: Type of elution model to fit to features

param.name: add_zeros
param.label: Add zero-intensity points outside the feature range to constrain the model fit
param.help: This parameter sets the weight given to these points during model fitting; '0' to disable

param.name: unweighted_fit
param.label: Suppress weighting of mass traces according to theoretical intensities when fitting elution models

param.name: no_imputation
param.label: If fitting the elution model fails for a feature, set its intensity to zero instead of imputing a value from the initial intensity estimate

param.name: each_trace
param.label: Fit elution model to each individual mass trace

section.name: check
section.title: Parameters for checking the validity of elution models (and rejecting them if necessary)

param.name: min_area
param.label: Lower bound for the area under the curve of a valid elution model

param.name: boundaries
param.label: Time points corresponding to this fraction of the elution model height have to be within the data region used for model fitting

param.name: width
param.label: Upper limit for acceptable widths of elution models (Gaussian or EGH), expressed in terms of modified (median-based) z-scores
param.help: '0' to disable. Not applied to individual mass traces (parameter 'each_trace')

param.name: asymmetry
param.label: Upper limit for acceptable asymmetry of elution models (EGH only), expressed in terms of modified (median-based) z-scores
param.help: '0' to disable. Not applied to individual mass traces (parameter 'each_trace')

param.name: max_iteration
param.label: Maximum number of iterations for EMG fitting

param.name: init_mom
param.label: Alternative initial parameters for fitting through method of moments

param.name: merge_features
param.label: For FAIMS data with multiple compensation voltages: Merge features that represent the same analyte detected at different CVs
param.help: Features are merged if they have the same charge and are within 5 seconds RT and 0.05 Da m/z. Intensities are summed

param.name: model_type
param.label: Options to control the modeling of retention time transformations from data

param.name: type
param.label: Type of model

param.name: symmetric_regression
param.label: Perform linear regression on 'y - x' vs
param.help: 'y + x', instead of on 'y' vs. 'x'

param.name: x_weight
param.label: Weight x values

param.name: y_weight
param.label: Weight y values

param.name: x_datum_min
param.label: Minimum x value

param.name: x_datum_max
param.label: Maximum x value

param.name: y_datum_min
param.label: Minimum y value

param.name: y_datum_max
param.label: Maximum y value

param.name: wavelength
param.label: Determines the amount of smoothing by setting the number of nodes for the B-spline
param.help: The number is chosen so that the spline approximates a low-pass filter with this cutoff wavelength. The wavelength is given in the same units as the data; a higher value means more smoothing. '0' sets the number of nodes to twice the number of input points

param.name: num_nodes
param.label: Number of nodes for B-spline fitting
param.help: Overrides 'wavelength' if set (to two or greater). A lower value means more smoothing

param.name: extrapolate
param.label: Method to use for extrapolation beyond the original data range
param.help: 'linear': Linear extrapolation using the slope of the B-spline at the corresponding endpoint. 'b_spline': Use the B-spline (as for interpolation). 'constant': Use the constant value of the B-spline at the corresponding endpoint. 'global_linear': Use a linear fit through the data (which will most probably introduce discontinuities at the ends of the data range)

param.name: boundary_condition
param.label: Boundary condition at B-spline endpoints: 0 (value zero), 1 (first derivative zero) or 2 (second derivative zero)

param.name: span
param.label: Fraction of datapoints (f) to use for each local regression (determines the amount of smoothing)
param.help: Choosing this parameter in the range .2 to .8 usually results in a good fit

param.name: auto_span
param.label: If true, or if 'span' is 0, automatically select LOWESS span by cross-validation

param.name: auto_span_min
param.label: Lower bound for auto-selected span

param.name: auto_span_max
param.label: Upper bound for auto-selected span

param.name: auto_min_neighbors
param.label: Minimum number of neighbors (span*n) enforced in auto mode

param.name: auto_k_folds
param.label: K-folds for CV when n>50 (else LOO is used)

param.name: auto_metric
param.label: Metric for CV selection: one of {'p90','p95','p99','rmse','mae'}

param.name: auto_span_grid
param.label: Optional explicit grid of span candidates in (0,1]
param.help: Comma-separated list, e.g. '0.2,0.3,0.5'. If empty, a default grid is used

param.name: num_iterations
param.label: Number of robustifying iterations for lowess fitting

param.name: delta
param.label: Nonnegative parameter which may be used to save computations (recommended value is 0.01 of the range of the input
param.help: e.g. for data ranging from 1000 seconds to 2000 seconds, it could be set to 10). Setting a negative value will automatically do this

param.name: interpolation_type
param.label: Method to use for interpolation between datapoints computed by lowess
param.help: 'linear': Linear interpolation. 'cspline': Use the cubic spline for interpolation. 'akima': Use an akima spline for interpolation

param.name: extrapolation_type
param.label: Method to use for extrapolation outside the data range
param.help: 'two-point-linear': Uses a line through the first and last point to extrapolate. 'four-point-linear': Uses a line through the first and second point to extrapolate in front and and a line through the last and second-to-last point in the end. 'global-linear': Uses a linear regression to fit a line through all data points and use it for interpolation

param.name: interpolation_type
param.label: Type of interpolation to apply

param.name: extrapolation_type
param.label: Type of extrapolation to apply: two-point-linear: use the first and last data point to build a single linear model, four-point-linear: build two linear models on both ends using the first two / last two points, global-linear: use all points to build a single linear model
param.help: Note that global-linear may not be continuous at the border

param.name: score_type
param.label: Name of the score type to use for ranking and filtering (.oms input only)
param.help: If left empty, a score type is picked automatically

param.name: score_cutoff
param.label: Use only IDs above a score cut-off (parameter 'min_score') for alignment?

param.name: min_score
param.label: If 'score_cutoff' is 'true': Minimum score for an ID to be considered
param.help: Unless you have very few runs or identifications, increase this value to focus on more informative peptides

param.name: min_run_occur
param.label: Minimum number of runs (incl
param.help: reference, if any) in which a peptide must occur to be used for the alignment.. Unless you have very few runs or identifications, increase this value to focus on more informative peptides

param.name: max_rt_shift
param.label: Maximum realistic RT difference for a peptide (median per run vs
param.help: reference). Peptides with higher shifts (outliers) are not used to compute the alignment.. If 0, no limit (disable filter); if > 1, the final value in seconds; if <= 1, taken as a fraction of the range of the reference RT scale

param.name: use_unassigned_peptides
param.label: Should unassigned peptide identifications be used when computing an alignment of feature or consensus maps
param.help: If 'false', only peptide IDs assigned to features will be used

param.name: use_feature_rt
param.label: When aligning feature or consensus maps, don't use the retention time of a peptide identification directly; instead, use the retention time of the centroid of the feature (apex of the elution profile) that the peptide was matched to
param.help: If different identifications are matched to one feature, only the peptide closest to the centroid in RT is used.. Precludes 'use_unassigned_peptides'

param.name: use_adducts
param.label: If IDs contain adducts, treat differently adducted variants of the same molecule as different

param.name: auto_reference
param.label: Reference to align to if none is given (neither a reference file nor an input index): 'best_run' - the input that shares the most identified sequences with every other input (on ties, the one with the most identified sequences)
param.help: A consensus is used instead if no input shares at least two sequences with every other input. If the chosen input leaves other inputs with too few alignment points, other inputs and a consensus are tried as well (see 'auto_reference_min_points'). 'consensus' - median RTs per sequence over all inputs. A consensus favors none of the inputs, but only partly corrects larger RT shifts, because every input contributes to the consensus it is aligned to

param.name: auto_reference_min_points
param.label: If 'auto_reference' is 'best_run': number of alignment points (after removing outliers, see 'max_rt_shift') that the reference should provide for every other input
param.help: If the chosen input leaves inputs with fewer points, and one of them shares at least this many sequences with other inputs, every input and a consensus of all inputs are tried as the reference. The choice that gives the most inputs at least this many points is used (the reference counts); on ties, the first choice is kept, and an input is preferred over a consensus. The default is the smallest number of points to which ProteomicsLFQ and MS1LabeledWorkflow fit an RT model. 0 disables the check

param.name: use_identifications
param.label: Never link features that are annotated with different peptides (only the best hit per peptide identification is taken into account)

param.name: nr_partitions
param.label: How many partitions in m/z space should be used for the algorithm (more partitions means faster runtime and more memory efficient execution)

param.name: min_nr_diffs_per_bin
param.label: If IDs are used: How many differences from matching IDs should be used to calculate a linking tolerance for unIDed features in an RT region
param.help: RT regions will be extended until that number is reached

param.name: min_IDscore_forTolCalc
param.label: If IDs are used: What is the minimum score of an ID to assume a reliable match for tolerance calculation
param.help: Check your current score type!

param.name: noID_penalty
param.label: If IDs are used: For the normalized distances, how high should the penalty for missing IDs be
param.help: 0 = no bias, 1 = IDs inside the max tolerances always preferred (even if much further away)

param.name: ignore_charge
param.label: false [default]: pairing requires equal charge state (or at least one unknown charge '0'); true: Pairing irrespective of charge state

param.name: ignore_adduct
param.label: true [default]: pairing requires equal adducts (or at least one without adduct annotation); true: Pairing irrespective of adducts

section.name: distance_RT
section.title: Distance component based on RT differences

param.name: exponent
param.label: Normalized RT differences ([0-1], relative to 'max_difference') are raised to this power (using 1 or 2 will be fast, everything else is REALLY slow)

param.name: weight
param.label: Final RT distances are weighted by this facto

section.name: distance_MZ
section.title: Distance component based on m/z differences

param.name: max_difference
param.label: Never pair features with larger m/z distance (unit defined by 'unit')

param.name: unit
param.label: Unit of the 'max_difference' paramete

param.name: exponent
param.label: Normalized ([0-1], relative to 'max_difference') m/z differences are raised to this power (using 1 or 2 will be fast, everything else is REALLY slow)

param.name: weight
param.label: Final m/z distances are weighted by this facto

section.name: distance_intensity
section.title: Distance component based on differences in relative intensity (usually relative to highest peak in the whole data set)

param.name: exponent
param.label: Differences in relative intensity ([0-1]) are raised to this power (using 1 or 2 will be fast, everything else is REALLY slow)

param.name: weight
param.label: Final intensity distances are weighted by this facto

param.name: log_transform
param.label: Log-transform intensities
param.help: If disabled, d = |int_f2 - int_f1| / int_max. If enabled, d = |log(int_f2 + 1) - log(int_f1 + 1)| / log(int_max + 1))

param.name: method
param.label: - top - quantify based on three most abundant peptides (number can be changed in 'top')
param.help: - iBAQ (intensity based absolute quantification), calculate the sum of all peptide peak intensities divided by the number of theoretically observable tryptic peptides (https://rdcu.be/cND1J). Warning: only consensusXML or featureXML input is allowed!

param.name: best_charge
param.label: Distinguish between fraction and charge states in detailed peptide output
param.help: For protein quantification, select one charge per modified peptide globally: maximize the number of (fraction group, label) assays with a positive abundance, then break ties by total abundance; retain that charge's values in every assay.. By default, protein abundances are summed over all charge states. How the retained values of several fractions are combined is governed by 'fractions:aggregate', not by this flag

section.name: top
section.title: Additional options for custom quantification using top N peptides

param.name: N
param.label: Calculate protein abundance from this number of proteotypic peptides (most abundant first; '0' for all)

param.name: aggregate
param.label: Aggregation method used to compute protein abundances from peptide abundances

param.name: include_all
param.label: Include results for proteins with fewer proteotypic peptides than indicated by 'N' (no effect if 'N' is 0 or 1)

section.name: fractions
section.title: Options for combining the fractions of a fraction group

param.name: aggregate
param.label: How the fractions of one fraction group are combined into that group's (fraction group, label) assay values
param.help: - sum - add up every fraction, i.e. treat them as the parts of one separated sample that they are.. - best - keep a single fraction per peptide and fraction group and discard the others. The fraction is chosen ONCE per peptide, ranked by the number of labels in which it has a positive abundance and then by the total of those abundances (an exact tie keeps the lowest fraction number), and ALL of its labels are then taken from it. The choice is deliberately not made per label: taking one channel from one fraction and another channel from a different fraction would mix physical aliquots and destroy the reporter-ion ratios that isobaric quantification consists of.. Only the assay values are affected. Per-(file, channel) quantities are per fraction by definition and always report every file

section.name: consensus
section.title: Additional options for consensus maps (and identification results comprising multiple runs)

param.name: normalize
param.label: Scale peptide abundances so that the median of each (fraction group, label) assay matches the overall median
param.help: Abundances of zero count as 'not detected' and are left out of the medians; an assay without any positive abundance takes no part in the normalization

param.name: fix_peptides
param.label: Use the same peptides for protein quantification across all (fraction group, label) assays
param.help: With 'N 0',all peptides that occur in every assay are considered.. Otherwise ('N'), the N peptides that occur in the most assays (independently of each other) are selected,. breaking ties by total abundance (there is no guarantee that the best co-ocurring peptides are chosen!).. A peptide counts as occurring in an assay only where its abundance is positive: an abundance stored as zero means 'not detected' (e.g. an isobaric reporter below 'min_reporter_intensity'), not a measurement of absence

param.name: fdr
param.label: MBR FDR threshold (0.05=5%)

param.name: random_seed
param.label: Seed for the random number generator used to select decoy donors
param.help: A fixed seed makes results reproducible

param.name: min_decoys
param.label: Minimum number of MBR decoy transfers required before any transferred feature is kept
param.help: Transferred features are also dropped whenever the requested 'fdr' cannot be resolved by the available decoys (1/decoys > fdr). When transfers are dropped, only direct identifications are retained. A 'fdr' of 1.0 disables FDR control and keeps all transfers regardless of this value

param.name: max_training_points
param.label: Upper bound on the number of candidate transfers used to TRAIN the transfer-FDR SVM in each cross-validation fold (0 = unlimited)
param.help: Predictions and the FDR/q-values are always computed over ALL transfers, so this only bounds the SVM-fitting cost and does not change which transfers are scored. Runs with very many features per run can otherwise make the SVM grid search slow. When the cap is hit, a deterministic stratified subsample is used: both labelled classes (decoys and positives) are kept whole if they fit, otherwise the minority class is kept whole and the majority is score-spread sampled to fit the budget

param.name: max_difference
param.label: Never pair features with larger m/z distance (unit defined by 'unit')

param.name: unit
param.label: Unit of the 'max_difference' paramete

param.name: enabled
param.label: Use a LOCAL adaptive retention-time window for MBR candidate search instead of the single global RT window ('distance_RT:max_difference')
param.help: For each donor the expected acceptor RT is predicted from nearby peptides identified in BOTH runs (local alignment) and the search window is sized from the local RT scatter, sharpening the RT feature and removing much of the false in-window background. The window is widened adaptively if too few decoys are produced to resolve the FDR. Set 'false' to restore the legacy single global RT window

param.name: max_window
param.label: Maximum half-width (seconds) of the local RT window before adaptive widening (backstop cap on the data-driven width)

param.name: min_window
param.label: Minimum half-width (seconds) of the local RT window

param.name: anchor_window
param.label: Only peptides within this RT distance (seconds) of the donor are used as local-alignment anchors

param.name: anchors
param.label: Maximum number of anchor peptides per side used for the local RT prediction

param.name: sigma_scale
param.label: Local RT window half-width = this multiple of the local anchor RT-shift standard deviation

param.name: fallback_window
param.label: Half-width (seconds) used when fewer than two local anchors are available

param.name: auto
param.label: Estimate the local RT window scales (max_window, min_window, anchor_window, fallback_window) from the data instead of using the fixed values above, so one configuration adapts across short and long gradients
param.help: Derived from the RT-shift scatter of shared anchors and the anchor density; uses 'median_fwhm' as a physical lower guard when provided

param.name: median_fwhm
param.label: Chromatographic peak FWHM (seconds) used as a physical lower guard when 'auto' is enabled (0 = estimate window scales from RT residuals and anchor density only)
param.help: Set by the host tool (e.g. ProteomicsLFQ) which has raw-spectra context

param.name: rt_score
param.label: How the retention-time feature is used on the local RT path
param.help: 'raw': the raw |Δrt| is the SVM predictor (legacy). 'svm': a calibrated [0,1] RT-agreement score (FlashLFQ-style two-tailed CDF against the data-driven RT prediction-error distribution) replaces it as the SVM predictor. 'svm_and_mbr': as 'svm', and the calibrated score also enters the bootstrap geometric mean. Ignored unless 'enabled'
